text:
incident-bot: ALERT: PagerDuty page fired PD#4567 -> inference-runtime us-west-2 high tail latency + increased 5xx. Severity: page. Link: https://redwood.ops/pd/4567

Maya: acked and taking this one. oncall handover now.

Oliver: i can stay on the bridge for a few mins if needed, will handoff after 5. Maya you got it?

Maya: yup taking. opening bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridge/4567

Oliver: quick signal — latency spike started ~t-3m, looks correlated with a recent kvcache TTL change from the canary rollout. cache miss rate jumped to ~85% on seq>1024 traffic. 5xx rate ~2.1% (baseline 0.02%).

Maya: noted. action plan (short): 1) revert kvcache TTL patch on canary 2) scale inference pool for steady capacity 3) enable fallback model-variant (low-memory) to keep customers served.

Kevin: if you're rolling back, here's the safe command i ran in staging, use with care:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime --to-revision=42
```
I can execute if you want me to.

Tracy: pinging support/CS to get customer impact triage. @Support can you confirm any customer-facing errors?

Support: CTS-123 reported timeouts and partial failures for batch embeddings. ~2k failed requests in last 10m, severity high. CS already opened a ticket and alerted the AM.

Maya: ok i’ll run the rollback now and monitor p95/p99. Oliver — please prep scaling step.

pagerbot: PD#4567 -> acknowledged by Maya (owner: Maya). Notifying escalation policy.

Maya: rollback initiated (deploy rollback command sent). watching kube events and metrics.

Oliver: scaling pool from 3 -> 6 to absorb burst: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-runtime --replicas=6` (done).

Kevin: rollback completed, kube events show ReplicaSet switched to revision 42, no errors in deploy logs. eviction rate starting to drop.

Maya: p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~320ms within 4m of rollback. 5xx trending down to 0.15%. still watching for flapping.

Tracy: CS update -> CTS-123 reporting recovery around t+10m; sent proactive note explaining transient rollout-induced cache evictions, offered follow-up postmortem.

Maya: good. i'm going to mark "mitigation in place" and follow for 15 more mins. Oliver — do you want ownership for postmortem and follow-ups?

Oliver: taking ownership for the postmortem and follow-up tasks. i'll create the incident doc and assign infra to adjust TTL safeties and add a canary threshold alert.

Maya: handing off live ownership to Oliver. i'm stepping out of bridge in 2m.

incident-bot: PD#4567 -> currently no active pages in the last 2 minutes. Recommended: keep monitoring for 30m and close if stable.

Oliver: noted. i'll keep the bridge open for now and will ping infra for a controlled re-roll with stricter cache metrics. filing the incident now: https://redwood.incidents/4567/postmortem

Maya: thanks team. final status ping before i go: p95 320ms, 5xx 0.12%, kvcache miss rate down to 12%. closing my hands-on. :thumbsup:

Support: CS will follow up with the customer summary and include remediation ETA.

Oliver: handing tracked ownership to me for 24h post-incident. ping if any regression. wrapping bridge in 20m unless alerts return.

pagerbot: PD#4567 -> ownership transferred to Oliver (postmortem owner).

Maya: swish — nice quick team work, good catch on the TTL behavior.

Oliver: thanks all. i'll post the blameless draft in #postmortems and loop infra & releases.

incident-bot: thread archived by incident-bot after 30m of stability.
